newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - 1/2 point late-day rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - 1/2 point late-day rally.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices rose about 1/2 point Thursday, following a surging Treasury market higher in a late-day rally.
Traders said market gains were fueled by the end of the Treasury's $39.75 billion quarterly refunding auction. The government long bond rallied a point higher in late trading, to yield 6.63 percent.

Muni new issue pricings benefited from the strong market. JP Morgan Securities Inc, which won $250 million Illinois general obligation bonds in the day's largest competitive deal, said late in the day it had just one maturity left to sell, $25.6 million of 2002 bonds.
PaineWebber Inc Thursday set coupon levels on Oakland, Calif.'s $436 million taxable pension obligation bond deal.

Actively quoted muni issues included Dade County, Fla., water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026, bid at 5.58 percent net, or four basis points below Wednesday's level. At midday, bids were quoted at 5.60 percent net.
Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were bid at 5.60 percent net, down five basis points.
In futures, both the March U.S. Treasury bond contract and March municipals contract rose 30/32, to 113-11/32 and 117-6/32, respectively. The MOB spread was unchanged at 123 ticks.

Market participants said Friday's producer price index for January will be closely watched. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the figure to show a 0.3 percent rise overall and a 0.2 percent increase excluding food and energy prices.
Next week's new issues are expected to total $1.6 billion in 81 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $475 million in 52 sales. The largest is a $65 Arlington Independent School District, Texas, issue on February 20.
Negotiated sales total $1.2 billion in 29 offerings. The largest is a $247 million Hempstead Industrial Development Authority, N.Y., offering through Smith Barney inc.
